title: Alabama Leads All Schools With Players in Super Bowl 60 - NewsBreak
text:
By Dre Day ,
10 hours ago
On Sunday, February 8th, the Seattle Seahawks will face off against the New England Patriots for Super Bowl 60. Although this is an NFL game being played, the University of Alabama is being mentioned more often than not when it comes to this years’ superbowl.
Download the WALJ Mobile App Now Former Alabama Quarterback Jalen Milroe is currently a rookie on the Seahawks and will head to the Super Bowl at just 23 years old. Milroe won’t be the only former Crimson Tide player at the big game this year.
In fact, Alabama has seven former players on active rosters for the Super Bowl. This puts Bama in the lead for all college football programs with former players at the Super Bowl.
Alabama football players on the Seattle Seahawks
CB Josh Jobe (2018-21)
QB Jalen Milroe (2021-24)
FB Robbie Ouzts (2021-24)
DL Jarran Reed (2014-15)
Alabama football players on the New England Patriots
DL Christian Barmore (2018-20)
TE CJ Dippre (2023-24)
LB Anfernee Jennings (2016-19)
No matter what, Bama will walk away from Super Bowl 60 with a championship ring.
Despite talk this past season, the SEC is still reigning supreme in the NFL with a total of 30 players at the big game. As far as the Crimson Tide is concerned, the historical numbers continue to favor the Tide.
Alabama has produced a total of 54 Super Bowl champions in the history of the NFL. Only USC and Penn State.
We will all be watching and waiting to see which former Alabama players will be crowned champions on the 8th. Roll Tide!

Tuscaloosa Tables Vote on Tax Incentive to Demolish Homes for New Restaurants & Stores The Tuscaloosa City Council voted on Tuesday to indefinitely table a vote on granting a tax incentive for a developer to demolish two dozen homes and build a shopping center featuring new-to-market restaurants and retailers. Businessman & Former Football Pro Enters Race for Tuscaloosa Council Seat A businessman and former professional athlete whose team won the Canadian equivalent of the Super Bowl in the 90s has thrown his hat in the race for a vacant seat on the Tuscaloosa City Council. (Stephen Dethrage | Tuscaloosa Thread) 7.
